title: India Tells Pakistan at UNHRC Geneva to Focus on Its Loans, Not 'Theatrics,' Cites 1990 Pandit Exodus and Minority Persecution
detail: Exercising India's right of reply at the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva on September 24, 2026, Indian envoy Kshitij Tyagi dismissed Pakistan's remarks on Jammu and Kashmir as 'historical revisionism, invented statistics and sectarian insinuation,' asserting J&K 'was, is and will always remain an integral and inalienable part of India' and that Pakistan should 'vacate' the parts of J&K it illegally occupies. Tyagi said neither territorial ambitions 'nor its theatrics in the Council' would help Pakistan 'repay the loans its economy survives on.' He cited the 1990 exodus of Kashmiri Pandits as the work of 'Pakistan-sponsored terrorists' and alleged systemic persecution of Pakistan's own minorities — Hindus, Sikhs and Christians whose populations have 'shrunk drastically since the formation of the country,' plus Shia, Ahmadiyya and Ismaili Muslims — including abduction and forced conversion of minority women and blasphemy-law intimidation. No Pakistani rebuttal had been reported as of September 24.

confidenceReason: On-record statement by a named Indian envoy at a public UN session, reported with direct quotes by a Tier-2 Indian outlet; no independent confirmation yet of a Pakistani response, which the entry notes as absent rather than assuming silence.

title: Pakistan-Administered Kashmir's Assembly Elects PML-N's Najeeb Naqi Khan President as Broadband Returns After 99-Day Blackout, Unrest Toll Still Contested
detail: Members of Azad Jammu and Kashmir's 53-seat Legislative Assembly voted September 24, 2026 at the Muzaffarabad secretariat to fill the presidency, vacant since President Sultan Mehmood Chaudhry's death on January 31 — nearly eight months beyond the constitutional deadline. Chief Election Commissioner Justice Ghulam Mustafa Mughal ruled that seven still-vacant seats (voting postponed in two districts on security grounds) did not bar the poll, since the winner needs only 27 of the 46 filled seats' votes; ruling PML-N and its allies control 32. PML-N's Najeeb Naqi Khan was expected to win. The vote came as broadband/DSL service was restored across AJK on September 13 after a 99-day suspension dating to the June 5 ban on the Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JKJAAC), though 3G/4G mobile data remained unavailable for several additional days — a partial, phased restoration rather than the full return implied by some September 15-21 reporting that described the blackout as still 'ongoing.' JKJAAC-led protests over the summer, demanding abolition of AJK's 12 refugee-reserved assembly seats, left a death toll still in dispute: residents and rights groups cite over 50 dead, while the AJK government acknowledges at least seven police and paramilitary personnel killed but has not given an overall figure.

media.caption: AJK's Legislative Assembly votes to elect a new president in Muzaffarabad, September 24, 2026

confidenceReason: Corroborated by an international Tier-2 outlet (Al Jazeera) for the election and by a Pakistani Tier-2 outlet (Express Tribune) for the broadband restoration timeline; the overall unrest death toll remains explicitly contested between government and rights-group figures.
